headline: Revenue jumps on AI demand, one-time charge hits profit
summary_short: Marvell's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 9.0% q/q and 27.6% y/y to $2,417.8M on AI-driven data center demand, but net income fell to $34.5M (-91.3% q/q, -80.6% y/y) after a $331.8M non-cash fair-value charge on the Celestial AI acquisition's contingent consideration.
summary_long: Revenue rose 9.0% q/q and 28% y/y to $2,417.8M, led by data center (+27% y/y) on AI demand for electro-optics, custom, storage and switching products, partly offset by the divested automotive-ethernet business. Gross margin expanded 180bp y/y to 52.1% on better cost absorption. R&D and SG&A rose on Celestial AI and XConn acquisition-integration costs and headcount growth. Net income fell to $34.5M (vs $396.1M q/q) as a $331.8M non-cash fair-value increase on the Celestial contingent-consideration liability hit other income, partly offset by an $81.1M forward-stock-purchase-contract gain. Cash rose to $3.8B (+$1.2B q/q) after NVIDIA's $2.0B preferred-stock investment; Marvell returned $253.8M via buybacks and dividends.

drivers.explanation: Data center revenue rose 27% y/y on AI-related demand for electro-optics, custom, storage and switching products; communications and other revenue grew 29% y/y on normalizing customer inventory, partly offset by the divested automotive-ethernet business.
Gross margin rose 180bp y/y to 52.1% primarily due to better cost absorption from higher revenue, partially offset by a shift in product mix.

Operating income fell 15.4% q/q (still up 35.5% y/y) as R&D (+28% y/y, incl. $22.3M acquisition costs) and SG&A (+39% y/y, incl. $42.6M acquisition costs) rose on Celestial AI/XConn integration and headcount growth.

Net income fell 80.6% y/y and 91.3% q/q primarily due to a $331.8M non-cash increase in the fair value of the Celestial AI contingent-consideration liability, partly offset by an $81.1M gain on the forward stock purchase contract.

AI-driven data center demand and the NVIDIA preferred-stock investment underpinned the quarter; GAAP net income and EPS were depressed by a one-time non-cash contingent-consideration revaluation tied to the Celestial AI deal, not by operating weakness.
